Governing features: Preserve numerical conventions, physical metadata and framework derivatives through scattering workflows. Reviewed committed 2843a70..3571534 (now 7c5ae9d) (now d915e30); no execution or mutations.

Three concrete findings:

  1. [P2][bug] Periodic parity responses become mislabeled helicity. _framework.py:991–1001 constructs SMatrix without preserving tm.polarization; its constructor sets "helicity" at line 1045. Trigger: sphere_tmatrix(..., polarization="parity") → solve_periodic → to_smatrix. Channels already use parity at line 969, so subsequent physical illumination, fields and power interpret parity coefficients as helicity. Propagate polarization as cascade already does. High confidence.

  2. [P2][invariant] Framework plane waves change convention in negative-index media. _framework.py:473–475,494–499 evaluates angular coefficients/polarization using real unit direction, while only phases use physical wavevectors. With Material(-1+0.1j, -1+0.1j), direction [1,0,0], native wavenumber is -1+0.1j. Native polarization uses principal algebraic square roots, producing M_y=+i; unit direction produces M_y=-i (plane.rs:129–170). Framework fields and expansions consequently disagree with ordinary PlaneWave. Evaluate the native gauge using physical wavevectors while retaining the fixed-direction derivative contract, or explicitly reject this unsupported branch. High confidence from source; unexecuted.

  3. [P2][invariant] Polarization conversion silently projects incomplete bases. _framework.py:398–403 accepts a one-mode basis without its opposite-polarization partner. Converting a coefficient [1] to parity and back yields [0.5]: each transformation is the scalar 1/√2. TMatrix, PortWave and SMatrix conversion methods share this issue. The normal API rejects missing partners. Validate complete pairs at physical conversion boundaries or expand the destination basis. High confidence.

Feature fit / behavior model: Constructors and wrappers generally follow the intended explicit physics workflow. These findings concern newly introduced public composition paths.

Fail-fast / compatibility risks: Finding 3 silently changes the represented field; findings 1–2 violate numerical conventions independently of intentionally dropped upstream Python compatibility.

Residual risks: Normal-incidence dynamic-order derivatives are explicitly documented as requiring fixed ports for other-parameter optimization; not a finding. Tests, wheels and runtime reproductions were not run. No Git, PR or comment state changed.
